checks.axioms: #assert_axioms _root_.PolicySubmission.policy in Submission/PolicyCheck.lean: fails the build on native_decide (its compiled-evaluator axiom), sorry (sorryAx) or any declared axiom, so every band's side conditions really did go through the kernel
checks.correctness: Shor.policy_submission_correct_semiclassical_balanced; same declared success bound and trial count
checks.ir_agreement: Shor.Reflect.Readout.check: measured circuit agreement at the reference probes; Shor.Reflect.Balanced.balancedChecks: balanced arithmetic, including shallow 2048-bit probes
checks.ir_not_proved: Agreement with the emitted measured IR is checked at sampled instances, not proved for all widths.
checks.shrink_advisory: bands[].shrinks is Shor.Policy.bandShrinks: does this band's table shrink the operand width at every width the band covers? false means the recursion falls through to the schoolbook leaf somewhere in the band's own range, so the band is dead weight there. A performance warning, NOT an admissibility condition - the policy is correct either way
checks.side_conditions: per band: C1 length, C2 det ≠ 0 (proved from pairwise projective distinctness), C3 ordered point consumption + safe adds, C4 returns to start — all four proved for every band in Submission/PolicyTemplate.lean by the submitter and reduced by Lean's kernel at build time
checks.sorted: ShorPolicySubmission.sorted: the thresholds strictly decrease, closed by decide. This is the only obligation a policy adds on top of its bands' own C1-C4, and it is what makes band i cover [t_i, t_{i-1}) literally

extraction.note: a timed-out registry isDefEq counts as no match and falls back to structural translation; the evaluation tier above checked the result
extraction.probe_thresholds: where the scan shrinks each table (the default)

width_rule.formula: W = min(xw div k, zw div k); chunk j < k-1 has width W, the top chunk xw - (k-1)W (resp. zw); box: lower chunks [0, 2^W - 1], top chunk [-2^(t-1), 2^(t-1) - 1] ([0,0] if t = 0); demand(r) = max(-rowLo, rowHi + 1, 0) with rowLo/rowHi the coordinatewise min/max of sum_j r_j L_j over the box; D = max over rows and both operands; tight = 1 + (least e >= 0 with D <= 2^e); floor = 1 + max chunk width over both operands; nextWidth = max(tight, floor). Shor.exactSignedWidthOfWidths (Compiler/ExactWidth.lean).
